title: Tackling Occupational Diseases for a Healthier Workforce
what_it_is: Tackling Occupational Diseases for a Healthier Workforce

sections.label: Workplace fatal injury rate drop
sections.summary: The workplace fatal injury rate fell to 1.0 per 100,000 workers in 2023 and continued into the first half of 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Since then, thanks to the work put in by the Ministry of Manpower (MOM), the unions and our employers, our workplace fatal injury rate has dropped to 1.0 per 100,000 workers in 2023 and this continued into the first half of 2024.

sections.label: Reported occupational disease cases
sections.summary: MOM statistics show over 1,200 OD cases in 2023, up 17%, and about 473 in the first half of 2024, with the Labour Movement concerned about under-reporting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to national WSH statistics released by MOM, there were over 1,200 cases of OD reported in 2023, a 17% increase from 2022; and about 473 reported cases in the first half of 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The increase in the number of reported cases over the past two years is the result of ongoing efforts to detect OD cases through enhanced surveillance and increased awareness in reporting among doctors and employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: However, the Labour Movement is concerned that we have barely scratched the surface and that there remains significant under-reporting of OD cases in Singapore.

sections.label: Medical Examinations Regulations amendment proposal
sections.summary: The Medical Examinations Regulations differ from the Work Injury Compensation Act, so the First Schedule should be amended to expand mandatory health screenings to all high-risk industries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The policy position taken in the Medical Examinations Regulations differs from that of the Work Injury Compensation Act, which states that ODs can happen from any occupation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: We should therefore amend the First Schedule of the Medical Examinations Regulations by expanding mandatory health screenings to all high-risk industries.

sections.label: UK work-related musculoskeletal disorders estimate
sections.summary: The UK reported in 2024 an estimated 543,000 workers with work-related musculoskeletal disorders, a rate of 1,600 cases per 100,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Through these, the UK was able to report in 2024 that it had an estimated 543,000 workers suffering from work-related musculoskeletal disorders, or a rate of 1,600 cases per 100,000 workers.

sections.label: Thermal sensor posture surveillance pilot
sections.summary: With NTUC, they will pilot a surveillance programme using thermal sensors to detect improper postures of workers during their work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In collaboration with the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC), they will pilot a surveillance programme using thermal sensors to detect improper postures of workers during their work.

sections.label: WSH Council occupational disease guidelines
sections.summary: The WSH Council has guidelines on diagnosis and management of ODs, but they were last updated in 2015, 10 years ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The WSH Council currently has a set of guidelines on the diagnosis and management of ODs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: However, it has been 10 years since the guidelines were last updated in 2015.

sections.label: National Centre for Occupational Diseases
sections.summary: The speaker cites NUS and Singapore General Hospital clinics and proposes a national Centre of Excellence for Occupational Diseases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The Centre for Environmental and Occupational Health at the National University of Singapore and specialised clinics at Singapore General Hospital that focus on treating ODs, such as lung and skin conditions, are key examples.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I propose for the Government to consolidate our all current expertise in OD to create a national Centre of Excellence for Occupational Diseases.

sections.label: Enhanced Workplace Health Surveillance programme
sections.summary: MOM rolled out the Enhanced Workplace Health Surveillance programme in 2021 for diseases from noise or chemical exposure.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: For this purpose, MOM had in 2021, rolled out the Enhanced Workplace Health Surveillance programme to address two groups of occupational diseases, namely those caused by excessive exposure to noise or chemical hazards.

sections.label: Reported occupational diseases and inspections
sections.summary: Reported occupational diseases rose from 659 in 2021 to 1,229 in 2023, and targeted inspections began June 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: With the introduction of the Enhanced Workplace Health Surveillance programme, the number of ODs reported increased from 659 in 2021 to 1,229 in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Since June 2024, we have also commenced targeted inspections for industries, such as metal-working companies, where noise-induced deafness has been more prevalent since 2022.

sections.label: Government grants for safer workplaces
sections.summary: Eligible companies can apply for Government grants such as the Productivity Solutions Grant to adopt safer technological solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Eligible companies can apply for Government grants, such as the Productivity Solutions Grant, to adopt technological solutions that make our workplaces safer and healthier.

sections.label: Sub-committee on occupational disease prevention
sections.summary: The sub-committee will develop approaches to strengthen prevention and management of occupational diseases in high-risk industries.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The sub-committee will develop approaches to strengthen the prevention and management of occupational diseases, especially in high-risk industries.
